blurb: The home itself: its state, its call log and the whole-home doctor.
reasons: One doctor shape: the six doctors answer the same keys, so a UI draws them with one component and an agent reads them with one rule: {"ok":true}, or what was found and what could not be checked.
Why --with tree: a page that shows everything in the home needs one read that contacts nothing. Opening the Doctor page runs no doctor; it reads the tree and shows each thing as not checked.
Why the call log lives here: it is the home's own file. A machine's and a Sandbox's logs are read from their own families.

calls.note: creates the home; a current home is left as it is and answers unchanged:true. No [path]: the home is the folder LAYERFS_HOME names, else ~/.layerfs, as for every call. This build converts no older home (v20, owner 2026-11-19; MIG): a folder that is not a LayerFS 2.0 home (a layerfs.json of another layout, or anything but layerfs.lock, the integration folders and .DS_Store in a folder with no layerfs.json) is refused Unsupported with a fix that moves it aside (mv <home> <home>.old && layerfs home init) and is never written; a broken layerfs.json is refused and left untouched

calls.new_work: No new capability. `outcome` is `created` or `unchanged`, from today's `created` boolean; `unchanged` is new as a key; `version` is the build's version. No `created_at`: the home's own file (`layerfs.json`) records its layout and id and no time. An older home is refused, not converted (v20).

calls.note: + machine.platforms (--with platforms). Reads the home and changes nothing; it writes no call-log line. state is ready, or broken with reason: missing (no home yet, fix: layerfs home init) or reason: outdated (a folder that is not a LayerFS 2.0 home, which this build does not convert: fix: mv <home> <home>.old && layerfs home init); a layerfs.json it cannot read is reason: failed. generation is a number that moves when any record in the home is written: a UI polls it and re-reads only when it moves. A live read (--with live, or sandbox get) writes a record only when the state word or its reason changes, and that write moves it; observed_at is kept beside the record in an observation file it does not cover. It does not move when the owner of a recorded op dies (a dead owner's op is ignored on read, with no write), nor for a Workspace the home does not record. --with tree is the whole home from records only, with no machine contacted: every machine with its sqlite Stores and its Sandboxes, then the PostgreSQL Stores and the buckets. A node holds what the records hold: a machine its platform (and cpus, memory_bytes where it has them), a Store its engine and projects (bare names, as store get answers them; a PostgreSQL Store also its machines, the names of the machines attached to it), a Sandbox its project, image and workspaces (each {workspace, branch}), a bucket its provider. A node leaves state out when ready; the state is the last one its record holds, so a blocked_by can name engine_down, not_answering, missing or unreachable after a live read saw it. A project and a Workspace take their Store's or Sandbox's state. Workspaces are listed only where the home keeps their records (a Sandbox on native, or one reached directly); elsewhere the node says workspaces_not_listed:true while that machine is ready. On a stopped machine a Store and a Sandbox answer blocked with blocked_by naming the machine, and no Workspaces are listed. Leftovers are not a section here: LayerFS removes them itself where nothing owns them (v20). The long form's bundle.source says where the Linux bundle this build would deploy was found: env:LAYERFS_BUNDLE, runtime (an installed runtime's own, <runtime>/bundle/linux-<arch>/ beside <runtime>/bin/layerfs, chosen after LAYERFS_BUNDLE and before the cache) or cache

tree.help: everything in the home, from its records only: `machines` (each with its sqlite `stores` and its `sandboxes`), `stores` (the PostgreSQL Stores, which live on no machine) and `buckets`. A node holds what the records hold and no more: a machine {machine, platform, cpus, memory_bytes}; a Store {store, engine, projects}, and a PostgreSQL Store also `connections` (every side that connects, as `store get` answers them: this computer, then each machine with its own address, a reach seen or a Sandbox); a Sandbox {sandbox, project, image, workspaces}; a bucket {bucket, provider}; each with `state` and its companion when it is not ready. Each node's keys are in `nodes`

calls.new_work: `generation` is new: a counter kept in the home and moved under the home's lock by every record write (machines, Stores, projects, Sandboxes, the Workspaces the home records, buckets, saved logins). A live read writes a record only when the derived state word or its reason changes, so polling does not move it; `observed_at` goes to an observation file beside the record, outside the counter. An op whose owner died is ignored on read without a write, so the counter does not signal that. `state` with `reason` and `fix` is new: today `home.state` is `missing`, `current`, `needs_conversion` or `unknown`, and a home it cannot read is answered as `unknown`, not refused. `version` is new in the answer (the build has it). `--with tree` is new: one read of the home's records that derives each node's state as `machine get`, `store get` and `sandbox list` derive it without a probe, from the last state word and reason each record holds. A node carries only what records hold: a machine's `cpus` and `memory_bytes` (null where its record has none), a PostgreSQL Store's `connections` ({machine, url}; `machine` is null for the home's own address), a Sandbox's `image`, a bucket's `provider`. `--with platforms` is today's `machine.platforms` answer under `platforms`, with `platforms` as `items`, `kernel` as `route` and `options[].name` as `option`. Flattening: `home {path, state, layout, mode}` becomes the top-level `home` (the path), `state`, `layout` and `mode`; `bundle.dir` becomes `bundle.path`. `warnings` and `home.mode_ok` leave the answer: `bundle.present`, `bundle.matches` and `daemon.matches` carry the facts, and `home doctor` reports them as findings. `daemon` is null where this computer runs no native daemon, as today. `message` is the sentence behind a `broken` state (today's `HomeMissing` or `HomeNeedsConversion` warning text) and null when `ready`.

calls.new_work: The call moves from the `logs` family; the reader and its filters are today's. Changes to a row: `at` (milliseconds) to `logged_at`, `ms` to `duration_ms`, `lines` to `items`, `next` and `has_more` to `next_cursor`. `call` and `project` are new as keys: a line stores the call's `argv`, and the filters already derive both from it; `--op` becomes `--call`. Redaction is today's (byte counts in `argv`); the list of redacted arguments moves from one name list to each argument's `redact` field. `outcome` splits: today it is `ok` or the refusal code, with the result's word in `kind`; now the word is `outcome` and the code is `error`. `v` and `layer` leave the row. The default page is 200 lines (100 today).

calls.note: replaces the shell's layerfs doctor (no alias). Checks the home itself (this build, its prerequisites, the Linux bundle, the home folder and its layout, free disk, and every record in the home), then gives each machine, PostgreSQL Store and bucket its own shallow check. It goes no deeper: a Store on a machine and a Sandbox are machine doctor's. The records check (home.records) reads references between records, file modes, leases and half-finished operations, and its finding names the thing it is about, at any depth. Short: {"ok":true}, or findings and not_checked; a not_checked entry carries blocked_by or reason (timeout, busy, lost). A stopped machine is not a problem: its record and state are checked, and the checks that need it running do not apply. No option changes what it checks, and there is no --timeout (each thing has its own time budget), no leftovers (LayerFS removes them itself, v20). --progress sends one event per finished thing. The call repairs nothing and exits 0 once its report is made

calls.new_work: The table call and the one doctor shape are new: today `layerfs doctor` is a shell command outside the call table that answers two reports (the whole-home sweep `{ok, findings, leftovers}` and the per-target `{checks, findings, counts, ...}`). The home's own checks exist as the `host` target and are renamed `home.*` (`checks.home`, in the order they run); `host.bundle_hashes` and `host.remote`, which are always skipped today, are left out. `home.capacity` measures and applies no threshold today: a finding for a nearly full disk needs one, which is new. Outcomes map: `pass` to `ok`, `fail` to its finding's severity, `unknown` and `skipped` to `not_checked` with a `reason` (or left out when the check does not apply), `blocked` to `not_checked` with `blocked_by`. New work: running the shallow check of each machine, PostgreSQL Store and bucket inside this call (today one call is one target), each with its own time budget; one event per finished thing; a records finding named by the thing's own word (today `entity {kind, name}`). The leftover list leaves the report: LayerFS removes leftovers itself (v20).
